title: Reboot unresponsive system using SysRq
summary: Use the Magic SysRq key sequence to safely reboot a frozen Linux system. This is safer than holding the power button as it syncs disks and unmounts filesystems.
prerequisites: SysRq must be enabled (see 'Enable full SysRq key functionality').

steps.explain: Press and hold Alt. Press and release SysRq (or Print Screen). Then press and release each letter in the order R-E-I-S-U-B, waiting about 1 second between each.
steps.gui: Hold Alt, press Print Screen/SysRq, then press R, E, I, S, U, B in sequence.

rollback.explain: This action reboots the system. There is no rollback once the reboot starts.

warnings: This will force a reboot. Ensure you have saved your work if possible, though the system is likely unresponsive.
On some laptops, you may need to use Fn+SysRq or Ctrl+Alt+SysRq.
